\section{Certificate schema and trusted kernel}\label{app:certificate}

The primary JSON certificate has schema
\texttt{ym-paper02-exact-certificate-v1}.  Its theorem-critical fields are:
\begin{itemize}
\item the declared tree edge indices and selected retained row indices;
\item exact cell counts and rational ranks;
\item the claimed floor $1/25$, positivity flags, and pivot digests;
\item exact fractions for $r,t,M_1,M_2,M_3,\kappa,\eta,$ and $\tau$;
\item exact consequence bounds $3/80$, $1/80$, $1/16$, $1/3$, and $1/15$;
\item an explicit list of scope exclusions and a final
\texttt{all\_checks\_pass} flag.
\end{itemize}

The trusted computational kernel is Python's arbitrary-precision integer and
\texttt{Fraction} arithmetic, together with the short matrix-construction,
elimination, and factorization routines distributed in the supplement.
\texttt{hashlib} and \texttt{json} serialize the evidence but do not decide a
mathematical inequality.  The independent verifier replaces rational rank and
$LDL^{\mathsf T}$ by modular elimination and integer Bareiss elimination.

The heat-kernel image and normed-algebra inequalities are analytic leaves, not
computed suprema.  The primary verifier checks their rational propagation.
The separation is deliberate: a finite test suite is evidence that the
implementation matches its contract, while the proofs in
Appendix~\ref{app:heat-kernel} justify the analytic inputs.
